Definition: from G1418 and a compound of G1787 (meaning a bowel); a "dysentery":--bloody flux.
BiblicalUsage: Dysentery, the bloody flux, as the father of Publius lay sick with a fever and a bloody flux, and Paul went in, prayed, and laid his hands on him and healed him. The Greek text spells the sickness with a different ending, but it is the same disease Luke the physician names.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Luke the physician recorded the disease and the healing side by side, because the God who made the body can mend it.
